page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A4.Ax.48 is a bare-metal server configuration powered by the ARM64 AmpereOne-M processor family. The machine provides 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating performance interference from simultaneous multithreading. It features 768 GB of total system memory, providing an 8 GB per core memory allocation that positions the platform effectively for memory-intensive computations.

Local storage is bundled directly with the hardware, consisting of 3840 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Accelerators are omitted entirely, with zero dedicated GPUs installed. In addition, the bare-metal profile includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for direct network connectivity. The single-socket or multi-socket bare-metal deployment offers direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, ensuring predictable execution latency across all 96 ARM cores.

From an efficiency standpoint, the dense ARM64 architecture provides high thread density and significant memory capacity on dedicated silicon, lowering energy and resource contention relative to traditional virtualized instances. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of specialized x86 instruction sets, requiring workloads to be compiled specifically for ARM64 architectures.

BM.Standard.A4.Ax.48 is primarily suited for large in-memory databases, high-throughput key-value stores, distributed analytics nodes, containerized microservice backends, and high-concurrency web services requiring direct hardware performance with low-latency local NVMe storage.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A4.Ax.48 is a high-density bare-metal server driven by Ampere AmpereOne-M ARM64 processors. Designed without a hypervisor, it equips users with 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at one thread per core. The server offers 768 GB of system memory, matching an 8 GB per core ratio, along with 3840 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage for low-latency data access. There are no discrete GPUs included, focusing its raw silicon entirely on general-purpose and memory-centric throughput. By combining direct hardware access with substantial RAM allocation and high-speed local disk capacity, BM.Standard.A4.Ax.48 delivers stable and isolated execution for high-concurrency environments. It is well-fitted for memory-intensive databases, large-scale container platforms, high-throughput caching, and ARM-native enterprise microservices.
